verdict: Micron's revenue quadrupled to $41.5B as AI data centers bid memory prices sky-high — 85 cents of every sales dollar survived as gross profit, and net income hit $28.2B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago — the AI memory supercycle

segments.name: Cloud Memory
segments.note: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) stacked right beside AI processors in cloud servers — the scarcest, most valuable memory Micron makes.

segments.name: Core Data Center
segments.note: DRAM and NAND for conventional cloud and enterprise data-center servers.

segments.name: Mobile and Client
segments.note: Memory for smartphones, PCs and other consumer devices.

segments.name: Automotive and Embedded
segments.note: Memory for cars, factories and industrial equipment — smaller and steadier than the AI-driven units.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Small leftovers outside the four business units.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generations of DRAM, HBM and NAND memory.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams and the cost of running the company.

otherDetail: Interest income of $215M on Micron's growing cash pile plus $9M from equity investments, outweighed by $321M of other non-operating losses (foreign-exchange and debt-related items).

takeaways.title: The memory supercycle
takeaways.text: Revenue was four and a half times the year-ago quarter as AI builders scrambled for HBM and DRAM. Every business unit at least tripled.

takeaways.title: Almost pure profit at the top
takeaways.text: Gross margin hit 85% — memory prices rose far faster than the cost of making chips. A year ago the same margin was 38%.

takeaways.title: A $28B profit quarter
takeaways.text: Net income of $28.2B was fifteen times the year-ago quarter — and Micron still spent $7.1B on factories (capex) chasing the demand.

footerNote: Business-unit revenues are as reported by Micron; 'All other' is the small residual outside the four units.
